3	/// Float's launch view: ripple rings expanding from a single suspended mote.
4	///
5	/// Design intent — the ripple *is* the loading indicator. Nothing spins and
6	/// nothing counts, so an unknown load time never reads as a stall.
7	///
8	/// Rings and mote share one loop (`period`), which is what produces the
9	/// "breathing" cadence. Phase is derived from the timeline date rather than
10	/// held in view state, so the view stays consistent with the app's one-clock
11	/// rule; swap `now` for `AnimationClock.simTime` if that is already running
12	/// this early.
13	struct SplashView: View {
14	
15	    var tagline: String = "Finding a quiet part of the sky"
16	    var statusText: String = "Loading starmaps…"
17	    var showsProgress: Bool = true
18	
19	    /// Shared loop length for rings and mote.
20	    private let period: Double = 6.2
21	    private let ringCount = 3
22	    /// The rings are flattened — a surface seen at a shallow angle, not a bullseye.
23	    private let ringSize = CGSize(width: 520, height: 300)
24	    /// Exposed so the exit transition can carry the last ring past the window bounds.
25	    let ringScaleRange: ClosedRange<Double> = 0.24...1.75
26	
27	    var body: some View {
28	        TimelineView(.animation) { context in
29	            let now = context.date.timeIntervalSinceReferenceDate
30	            let loop = (now / period).truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1)
31	
32	            ZStack {
33	                starfield
34	
35	                ZStack {
36	                    // Static guide ring: keeps the composition from emptying out
37	                    // between pulses.
38	                    Ellipse()
39	                        .strokeBorder(Color(red: 0.55, green: 0.75, blue: 1).opacity(0.09), lineWidth: 1)
40	                        .frame(width: ringSize.width, height: ringSize.height)
41	
42	                    ForEach(0..<ringCount, id: \.self) { i in
43	                        let phase = (loop + Double(i) / Double(ringCount))
44	                            .truncatingRemainder(dividingBy: 1)
45	                        ripple(phase: phase, index: i)
46	                    }
47	
48	                    mote(loop: loop)
49	                }

What changed in `Float/App/SplashView.swift`:

I also corrected the comment in `SpatialImageEnvironment.swift:208` that justified the off-main decode by pointing at the splash animation — that animation no longer exists, but the off-main decode is still worth keeping on its own merits.

Every value in that view was driven by the main run loop, so anything animated there freezes and jumps for exactly as long as the upload blocks. Confirming which RealityKit call it is would need Instruments on device, and it wouldn't change the outcome for the splash either way.

**BUILD SUCCEEDED.** (SourceKit's "cannot find in scope" spray is the usual noise — it lost the module index; the compiler resolves all of it.)

The diagnosis was a timing race, not a colour problem. `maskedSwap` slept a fixed 0.30 s, called the swap, and returned — but the swap only *started* an async decode taking seconds. The flash meanwhile ran its fixed 0.82 s course and faded out on schedule, uncovering the sphere that was still mounted (the old sky). Seconds later the decode landed and `attach` cut to the new sky with no mask left. Exactly the three beats you saw: black → original → jump.

The fix makes the mask outlast the work instead of guessing at its duration:

- **`WhiteoutComponent.holding`** (`Float/Layers/DepthLayers.swift`) — while set, the overlay parks at full black and its clock is clamped to the end of `hold`, so release always drops straight into the fade-out no matter how long the wait ran. `hold` is now a *minimum*, not the whole peak.
- **`maskedSwap(to:)`** (`Float/App/AppModel.swift`) — kicks off `prepare(index:)` at the same instant as the fade-in, awaits it, waits for the overlay to actually be opaque, attaches, then clears `holding`. The reveal is now driven by the load finishing.
- The opacity wait polls the component's own `elapsed` rather than sleeping 0.25 s of wall clock, since the flash advances on the render clock — that mismatch is what made the original fixed sleep fragile in the first place.
- A failed load (`prepare` returns nil) still releases, fading back to the current sky rather than parking at black.
- `selectScene` now checks "swap in flight" *before* writing `currentScene`/UserDefaults. The in-flight window is a full decode now, so a second tap during it would previously have persisted a sky that never loaded.

One consequence worth deciding on: a scene change now sits at full black for the entire decode — seconds, not 0.82 s. That's the honest cost; the old version only felt shorter because it showed you the wrong sky. If that hold turns out to feel too long in the headset, the lever is the same one behind the splash stutter — the decode itself — and options there are pre-decoding the *next* sky speculatively, or putting a status line on the black the way the splash now does.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the four test planet/moon bodies as USDZ geometry for RealityKit.

Run under Blender, not bare python:

    /Applications/Blender.app/Contents/MacOS/Blender -b -P scripts/render_planets.py -- [--bake] [--only saturn]

WHY GEOMETRY AND NOT A PAINTED BACKDROP
    The sky HEICs sit at one near-infinite depth (depth_floor 0.94, ~0.2% baseline), so
    anything composited into the equirect has no parallax between the eyes. That is a large
    part of why the existing `saturn1` scene reads as a picture of space rather than a place.
    A body the viewer is supposed to feel near has to be real geometry with real stereo.

WHY CYCLES AND A BAKE (and only for Saturn)
    visionOS rejects RealityKit's `CustomMaterial` — only `ShaderGraphMaterial` authored in
    Reality Composer Pro, no hand-written Metal — so the app cannot render the two shadows
    that sell Saturn: the ring shadow banding the globe, and the globe's shadow thrown across
    the rings. Those get ray-traced here and baked into the colour map. Bake the LIGHTING,
    never the geometry: stereo parallax has to stay real, and a body that rotates once per
    ~10.6 h can afford frozen lighting. Jupiter, Venus and Iapetus have no self-shadowing
    feature to capture, so they ship unbaked and keep a live RealityKit light.

Stage 1 (always) exports plain textured USDZ for every body — fast, and enough to judge scale
and sharpness in the headset. Stage 2 (`--bake`) is the Saturn ring/globe shadow bake, which
is slow and the part most likely to need iterating; a stage-2 failure still leaves stage 1's
output on disk.
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import bpy  # noqa: E402  (only importable inside Blender)

SRC = Path("/Volumes/Logic Pro/FloatScratch/planets")
OUT = Path("/Volumes/Logic Pro/FloatScratch/planets/usdz")

# Sphere tessellation. 256x128 is well past what silhouette-smoothness needs at these angular
# sizes; the cost is trivial next to the textures and it keeps the limb from faceting when a
# body fills a large part of the view.
SEGMENTS, RINGS = 256, 128

# Axial tilt (degrees) applied about X so the poles do not sit dead vertical — a body lit and
# tilted reads as a world, a body square-on reads as a sticker. Venus is retrograde (177°),
# which is why its "north" ends up nearly upside down; that is correct, not a bug.
BODIES = {
    "iapetus": {"map": "iapetus_map_8192.png", "tilt": 15.5},
    "jupiter": {"map": "jupiter_map_8192.png", "tilt": 3.1},
    "saturn":  {"map": "saturn_map_8192.png",  "tilt": 26.7, "rings": True},
    "venus":   {"map": "Solarsystemscope_texture_8k_venus_surface.jpg", "tilt": 177.4},
}

# Saturn's rings, in globe radii. C ring inner edge to A ring outer edge.
RING_INNER, RING_OUTER = 1.235, 2.27
RING_ALPHA = "Solarsystemscope_texture_8k_saturn_ring_alpha.png"
RING_SEGMENTS = 512

# Sun placement. Off to one side and slightly above so there is a terminator to read depth
# from, but not so oblique that most of the body is unlit.
SUN_EULER = (0.0, 0.98, 0.60)   # radians
BAKE_SIZE = 4096


def log(msg):
    print(f"[planets] {msg}", flush=True)


def reset_scene():
    bpy.ops.wm.read_factory_settings(use_empty=True)
    scene = bpy.context.scene
    scene.render.engine = "CYCLES"
    # Metal GPU if this machine exposes one; Cycles falls back to CPU on its own if not.
    try:
        prefs = bpy.context.preferences.addons["cycles"].preferences
        prefs.compute_device_type = "METAL"
        prefs.get_devices()
        for dev in prefs.devices:
            dev.use = True
        scene.cycles.device = "GPU"
    except Exception as exc:                      # noqa: BLE001 - informational only
        log(f"GPU unavailable ({exc}); using CPU")
    scene.cycles.samples = 256


def add_sun():
    bpy.ops.object.light_add(type="SUN", location=(0, 0, 0))
    sun = bpy.context.object
    sun.rotation_euler = SUN_EULER
    sun.data.energy = 4.0
    # A real sun is not a point at this distance, and a hard-edged ring shadow looks CG.
    # ~0.53° is the sun's actual angular diameter from Earth; from Saturn it is far smaller,
    # but a little penumbra reads better than a razor edge.
    sun.data.angle = 0.009
    return sun


def make_globe(name, map_path, tilt_deg):
    bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add(segments=SEGMENTS, ring_count=RINGS, radius=1.0)
    globe = bpy.context.object
    globe.name = name
    bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()
    # The UV sphere primitive's default unwrap is already equirectangular (u wraps longitude,
    # v runs pole to pole), which is exactly how these maps are authored — no reprojection.
    globe.rotation_euler = (tilt_deg * 3.14159265 / 180.0, 0, 0)

    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(f"{name}_mat")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    tex = mat.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")
    tex.image = bpy.data.images.load(str(map_path))
    # Colour maps are authored in sRGB; the default guess is right for jpg but be explicit so
    # the png-vs-jpg sources cannot end up graded differently from each other.
    tex.image.colorspace_settings.name = "sRGB"
    mat.node_tree.links.new(bsdf.inputs["Base Color"], tex.outputs["Color"])
    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 0.9   # no specular hotspot on a rock or a cloud deck
    bsdf.inputs["Metallic"].default_value = 0.0
    globe.data.materials.append(mat)
    return globe, mat, tex


def make_rings(name):
    """Flat annulus with radial UVs.

    The SSS ring texture is a strip (8192x~500) where the X axis IS radial position, so the
    unwrap has to map u = normalised radius rather than anything the automatic unwrappers
    would produce. Building the mesh by hand is the short path to that.
    """
    import bmesh

    mesh = bpy.data.meshes.new(f"{name}_rings")
    obj = bpy.data.objects.new(f"{name}_rings", mesh)
    bpy.context.collection.objects.link(obj)

    bm = bmesh.new()
    uv_layer = bm.loops.layers.uv.new()
    import math
    inner, outer = [], []
    for i in range(RING_SEGMENTS):
        a = 2 * math.pi * i / RING_SEGMENTS
        inner.append(bm.verts.new((math.cos(a) * RING_INNER, math.sin(a) * RING_INNER, 0)))
        outer.append(bm.verts.new((math.cos(a) * RING_OUTER, math.sin(a) * RING_OUTER, 0)))
    bm.verts.ensure_lookup_table()
    for i in range(RING_SEGMENTS):
        j = (i + 1) % RING_SEGMENTS
        face = bm.faces.new((inner[i], outer[i], outer[j], inner[j]))
        # u: 0 at the inner edge, 1 at the outer edge. v is unused by a 1-D strip.
        for loop, u in zip(face.loops, (0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.0)):
            loop[uv_layer].uv = (u, 0.5)
    bm.to_mesh(mesh)
    bm.free()

    mat = bpy.data.materials.new(f"{name}_rings_mat")
    mat.use_nodes = True
    mat.blend_method = "BLEND"
    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    tex = mat.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")
    tex.image = bpy.data.images.load(str(SRC / RING_ALPHA))
    tex.extension = "EXTEND"   # never wrap: sampling past the outer edge must not fetch the C ring
    mat.node_tree.links.new(bsdf.inputs["Base Color"], tex.outputs["Color"])
    mat.node_tree.links.new(bsdf.inputs["Alpha"], tex.outputs["Alpha"])
    bsdf.inputs["Roughness"].default_value = 1.0
    obj.data.materials.append(mat)
    return obj


def export_usdz(objects, path):
    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")
    for o in objects:
        o.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = objects[0]
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    bpy.ops.wm.usd_export(
        filepath=str(path),
        selected_objects_only=True,
        export_textures=True,
        relative_paths=False,
generate_preview_surface=True,
    )
    log(f"wrote {path.name} ({path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)")


def build(body, do_bake):
    spec = BODIES[body]
    map_path = SRC / spec["map"]
    if not map_path.exists():
        log(f"SKIP {body}: missing {map_path.name}")
        return
    log(f"=== {body} ({map_path.name}) ===")
    reset_scene()
    add_sun()
    globe, mat, tex = make_globe(body, map_path, spec["tilt"])
    objects = [globe]
    if spec.get("rings"):
        rings = make_rings(body)
        rings.rotation_euler = globe.rotation_euler   # rings sit in the equatorial plane
        objects.append(rings)

    export_usdz(objects, OUT / f"{body}.usdz")

    if do_bake and spec.get("rings"):
        log(f"{body}: baking ring/globe shadowing at {BAKE_SIZE} (slow)")
        bake_shadows(globe, mat, tex, body)
        export_usdz(objects, OUT / f"{body}_baked.usdz")


def bake_shadows(globe, mat, tex, name):
    """Bake COMBINED lighting into a new map so the ring shadow survives export.

    This is the only reason Blender is in this pipeline at all. RealityKit on visionOS cannot
    be made to cast the ring shadow onto the globe, so it gets painted in.
    """
    img = bpy.data.images.new(f"{name}_baked", BAKE_SIZE, BAKE_SIZE // 2)
    target = mat.node_tree.nodes.new("ShaderNodeTexImage")
    target.image = img
    # Cycles bakes into whichever image node is ACTIVE — not the one that is linked. The
    # source texture stays wired to Base Color so its colour is part of what gets baked.
    mat.node_tree.nodes.active = target

    scene = bpy.context.scene
    scene.cycles.bake_type = "COMBINED"
    scene.render.bake.use_pass_direct = True
    scene.render.bake.use_pass_indirect = True
    scene.render.bake.margin = 16

    bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")
    globe.select_set(True)
    bpy.context.view_layer.objects.active = globe
    bpy.ops.object.bake(type="COMBINED")

    out = OUT / f"{name}_baked.png"
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    img.filepath_raw = str(out)
    img.file_format = "PNG"
    img.save()
    log(f"baked -> {out.name}")

    # Swap the baked map in so the follow-up export carries it.
    bsdf = mat.node_tree.nodes["Principled BSDF"]
    for link in list(mat.node_tree.links):
        if link.to_socket == bsdf.inputs["Base Color"]:
            mat.node_tree.links.remove(link)
    mat.node_tree.links.new(bsdf.inputs["Base Color"], target.outputs["Color"])


def main():
    argv = sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--") + 1:] if "--" in sys.argv else []
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--only", help="build a single body (%s)" % ", ".join(BODIES))
    ap.add_argument("--bake", action="store_true", help="also run the slow Saturn shadow bake")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    todo = [args.only] if args.only else list(BODIES)
    for body in todo:
        if body not in BODIES:
            log(f"unknown body {body}")
            continue
        try:
            build(body, args.bake)
        except Exception as exc:                  # noqa: BLE001 - one body failing must not
            log(f"FAILED {body}: {exc}")          # take the rest of the batch down
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()
    log("done")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Entertainment: real browser, in-app Music, honest Watch labels; planet USDZ

Browser (replaces the single-page Kindle reader, WebReaderPanel.swift):
- Tabs, each keeping its own WKWebView for the window's lifetime so switching
  preserves scroll position, form state and JS context.
- Session restore — reopens the tabs that were open, on the tab that was in
  front. That IS the "default to the last page used": no home page needed.
- History with search and clear, deduped by URL so repeat visits update one row
  instead of stacking forty copies of the same page.
- Address bar that takes a URL or a search. "Plausibly a URL" = has a scheme, or
  has a dot and no spaces, which keeps `read.amazon.com` working bare without
  turning `swift concurrency` into a hostname.
- One shared persistent data store across all tabs, so a passkey/Optic ID login
  happens once and survives relaunch.
- target=_blank links load in the requesting tab rather than silently doing
  nothing, which is the usual "this link is broken" bug in an embedded web view.

iCloud Tabs: NOT possible. Safari's iCloud tab list has no public API. Handoff
(NSUserActivityTypeBrowsingWeb) is the supported equivalent and is wired up: with
Safari frontmost on a Mac or iPhone, Float appears in the Dock and opens that
page in a new tab.

Music: MusicKit, played in-process via ApplicationMusicPlayer — library
playlists/albums, catalog search, now-playing transport. Launching Music.app tore
down the immersive space (visionOS makes it exclusive), so changing a track meant
leaving deep space. Playback state is read from the player's own ObservableObject
rather than mirrored, since it changes for reasons this app never sees.
REQUIRES the MusicKit capability on the Ash4d.Float App ID at developer.apple.com
— code alone cannot enable it.

Watch: the Apple TV app's library has no public API; its titles are FairPlay-
protected and decrypt only inside that app. Rather than a "TV Library" button
that could only fail, the section names its two working sources — local video
from Photos, and tv.apple.com/streaming sites via the browser.

scripts/render_planets.py: Blender → USDZ for Iapetus/Jupiter/Saturn/Venus as
real geometry (a body composited into the equirect gets no parallax — a large
part of why saturn1 reads as a picture). Saturn additionally Cycles-bakes the
ring shadow onto the globe at 8192, since visionOS rejects CustomMaterial and
RealityKit cannot cast it.
